seal.statement: Preparing a private writable transaction workspace must not require copying, serializing, scanning, or rewriting the complete partition state before the transaction can proceed. Workspace startup cost must be bounded by transaction/workspace activity rather than total historical partition size, while preserving the SQL semantics promised by the distributed-transaction contract. A fresh verifier proves on a reference host and a slower supported lab host that a very-large-base/tiny-fixed-transaction series is fleet-safe under the audited liveness budget and insensitive to unrelated database growth, while a small-base/large-transaction series attributes legitimate cost to transaction work; authoritative apply remains healthy, pre-commit effects remain private, intended SQLite semantics and deterministic effects are retained, memory/temp-disk/handle/cleanup state are bounded, crash cleanup is safe, and the mechanism has one semantic owner and one lifecycle.

text: Owner accepted the distributed-transaction design STOP at 292b7204334cf47617e675dd9b12bc708b682886. Full serialization plus WAL-header normalization is functional and the finalized harness is green, but O(total partition bytes) workspace preparation is rejected independently of Raft-history compaction, total-partition caps, split thresholds, host throughput, or budget inflation. The stopped transaction design resumes only after this prerequisite is proven.

Budget audit correction: 350 ms is retained as the stopped gate's historical assumption but is not a source-owned rs-raft election budget at 292b720433. Default partition timing reaches rs-raft and derives 1000/3500/6000 ms core minima before randomization. The actual liveness constraint is residual follower-election slack consumed by uninterrupted authoritative event-loop/tick/Ready/send monopoly; off-thread workspace readiness may be longer if authoritative apply continues and the exact snapshot remains valid. This does not rescue O(total partition bytes) serialization.

Read-only mechanism challenge: no existing primitive provides an exact current writable SQLite branch with startup independent of total state. B is unavailable on the current binding, C is a non-portable accelerator without an acceptable fallback, D monopolizes or joins the authoritative writer, E cannot preserve the retained SQL language with sound minimal dependencies, and F creates a second state owner. Page-level COW/VFS remains an unproven theory whose first binary probe is exact applied-index/WAL rooting without total enumeration.

Sealed the immutable 292b720433 STOP handoff, recorded two independent read-only challenges and the liveness correction, and built the pre-implementation complexity falsifier. Its dense 8/64/256 MiB fixed-transaction series and small-base/4096-row case use byte/page counters to reject full serialization independently of host speed while separately reporting six phases and SQLite semantic checks. No production src path changed.

Pre-implementation falsifier calibrated green at exact head ce067f4f865ab47261cafecfdc607efb662e92ff. Dense 8/64/256 MiB fixed-transaction fixtures produced a 31.89x database-size and creation-byte slope, so full serialization was rejected as O(total-partition-bytes) without timing. Through the lab controller, tv-dator passed the falsifier 37 assertions in 1038 ms and lenovo-laptop passed 37 in 1679 ms; both exclusive lanes were 4/4 files and 82 assertions green. This validates the witness only; all ten candidate receipts remain red.

Static and corpus ratchets passed, but the exact-checkout whole-corpus gate repeatedly failed transaction-concurrent-read-outage formation on tv-dator; nothing was pushed and origin has no quest ref. Read-only Gate A challenge: applied index I read inside the same pinned WAL read transaction exactly identifies the atomic application-state projection and remained stable through same-page live writes and checkpoint pressure. Current better-sqlite3 cannot expose pager pages; Gate A remains open for a probe-only SQLITE_ENABLE_DBPAGE_VTAB lazy-page witness. Retained WAL, reader marks, autocheckpoint cost and release are required resource measurements.

Read-only ownership/performance challenge: no universal 350 ms workspace timeout. Measure synchronous authoritative event-loop/tick monopolization against each follower's residual randomized election interval separately from executor wall time. A future workspace must be disposable and non-authoritative; hidden base/WAL scans, whole-file finalization, unbounded WAL retention, another pager/WAL owner or recovery/reconciliation are STOP conditions.

Recorded the failed exact-HEAD STOP-branch publication without bypassing the red corpus gate, preserved both independent read-only COW challenges, and merged them into an immutable-base Gate A amendment. Gate A authorizes only a probe-only pinned-pager/page-export witness; no writable overlay and no production src change were made.

Built the Gate A1 probe-only DBPAGE witness without changing production SQLite flags. The shipped better-sqlite3 runtime lacks DBPAGE and snapshot APIs; a disposable process compiled from the vendored amalgamation pins I on its own read connection and lazily resolves selected pages. Across 8/64/256 MiB fixtures, database pages grew 31.875x while requests/materialized bytes stayed 2/8192. Same table/index bytes and a late-first-access page stayed at I through 128 writes and checkpoint pressure; releasing the reader restored TRUNCATE. Thirty-two independently aged readers retained exact acquisition indices, disproving a presumed five-workspace limit. Gate A remains open because real Raft tick/apply liveness and a production exposure design are unproven; no overlay or src change was made.
